Safety is an engineering problem, the @nvidia edition:

Open Shell to enforce policy in the kernel outside the agent process. Can be paired with Sentry which runs in BF-4 and can quarantine a rogue agent in milliseconds.

Containment is the backstop to alignment. Super elegant. https://t.co/eEh6T6H5uz

Nvidia’s new Open Agent Safety Platform would have probably prevented the much discussed Hugging Face incident.

Engineering a better, safer world.

quoted.text: From what we know (take with a grain of salt, we need much more transparency!), if @OpenAI had been running this on their own agents that attacked us, they would have caught them before we did! Since the first agent cyberattack hit us in July, we've been asking what safe agent infra actually needs. Our current read: the destinations were allowed, the payloads weren't. By OpenAI's own account the agents turned an allowed package repository into a message board. Allowlists alone restrict where an agent can go, not what it does. So here's our first contribution to OpenShell, part of the just launched @nvidia Open Agent Safety Platform: monitoring of the traffic you already allow. - Network budgets per sandbox (requests, writes, bytes) - Drift versus each sandbox's baseline and the cohort - Fleet view: many sandboxes suddenly writing to one host raises a finding, even if every single request is allowed In the demo below, 4 sandboxed agents coordinate through a software repository they're all allowed to use. 0 rules broken, caught in minutes. That fleet view is exactly the message board pattern from July. OpenShell: https://t.co/ZbDANrZsm6 Our proof of concept: https://t.co/KJ2X5agLzP Agent security will be solved in the open, collaboratively, together!
